headword: {新社会人|しんしゃかいじん}
gloss: new member of the workforce; fresh graduate entering society

definitions.gloss: new member of the workforce; person who just started working
definitions.explanation: A person who has recently graduated from school and entered the workforce for the first time. In Japan, this typically refers to the cohort of graduates who start their jobs in April.

examples.japanese: ⟦{四月|しがつ}→四月：00668_shigatsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{新社会人|しんしゃかいじん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I'll be entering the workforce starting in April.

examples.japanese: {新社会人|しんしゃかいじん}⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧だ。
examples.english: The first month is tough for new members of the workforce.

examples.japanese: {新社会人|しんしゃかいじん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}けた→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧⟦ビジネス→ビジネス：11162_bijinesu⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本|ほん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{出版|しゅっぱん}→出版：03222_shuppan⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Many business etiquette books aimed at new members of the workforce are published.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{新社会人|しんしゃかいじん} reflects Japan's synchronized hiring system, where most companies hire fresh graduates (⟦{新卒|しんそつ}→新卒：12871_shinsotsu⟧) and start them on April 1st. The spring season features many advertisements and products marketed to {新社会人|しんしゃかいじん}, from suits and business bags to self-help books.

ETYMOLOGY:
{新|しん} (new) + ⟦{社会人|しゃかいじん}→社会人：13730_shakaijin⟧ (member of society / working adult). The term ⟦{社会人|しゃかいじん}→社会人：13730_shakaijin⟧ itself distinguishes working adults from students.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}→新入社員：15536_shinnyuushain⟧ (new employee — more specific to a company)
- ⟦{新卒|しんそつ}→新卒：12871_shinsotsu⟧ (fresh graduate)
- ⟦{社会人|しゃかいじん}→社会人：13730_shakaijin⟧⟦{一年生|いちねんせい}→一年生：27559_ichinensei⟧ (first-year working adult — informal)
